title: Clip 1:
title_short: Gala · Clip 1 · Cheryl Little founder piece
headline: Miami grew with immigrants, and for thirty years Americans for Immigrant Justice grew with them, from two sisters and Cheryl to the city’s legal defense.
story: Clip 1 of the gala. It opens on Cheryl: the people AIJ helped built businesses, one became an immigration attorney, and they are not the worst of the worst. Then the narrator shows the Miami they built.

Cheryl tells the founding in her own words: two sisters, “we’ve got to start our own agency”, the Miami office in 1996, growing fast. The narrator gives the stakes, Sui says Miami would look very different without AIJ, and the film ends on “Immigrants built it.” Warm, upbeat and proud, never angry.
do: Open on Cheryl’s bite at 0:00 with the hook text already on screen. Andrés approved this opener: do not move it back into script order.
Keep the music upbeat from frame 1: start the track at its own 0:59 and keep that energy to the end. Keep it 18 to 20 dB under every voice.
Cover talking heads after a few seconds with relevant B-roll: Miami people, Little Havana, Little Haiti, the people AIJ has helped.
Use the historic AIJ footage wherever the story is about the past, with a film-grain or old-TV look so it reads as archive.
Keep the grade and the clean, vibrant B-roll look Andrés praised.
dont: No amount of money in any line. Cheryl’s Miami office line stops at “1996”.
No private YouTube footage. News footage only with the outlet’s credit or logo visible. Otherwise our footage or Andrés’ Miami B-roll.
No food stereotypes, no shots that read as Cuba or another city, no person being dragged, no blurred client, no woman in the white blouse.
No interviewer audio. No “Well” before “In 1995”. No narration line “Thirty years ago, Miami needed a voice for the people…”.
No AIJ or FIAC logo before the end card. No Paul as the face of “three decades”.

Restaurants and coffee shops started by families. A skyline that keeps reaching new heights.

voice.quote: Miami has grown tremendously over the last 30 years. We’re a different city than we were 30 years ago. I truly believe that if it weren’t for Americans for Immigrant Justice and the support that we’ve given to so many vulnerable communities … Miami would look very different. The brilliance, the success, the transformation of our city would look very different if it weren’t for Americans for Immigrant Justice really fulfilling the need in the community.

checklist: Frame 1 is Cheryl with the hook text already on. No logo, no name, no fade.
Cheryl’s name super comes at 00:03 or later: Cheryl Little / Co-Founder, Americans for Immigrant Justice.
No amount of money anywhere. The Miami office line ends on “1996”.
The stakes line says: “Most immigrants facing deportation do not have legal representation.” Narration and captions match.
No “Well” before “In 1995”. No “Thirty years ago, Miami needed a voice…” narration.
Music starts at the upbeat part and stays upbeat. It sits well under every voice.
Every B-roll shot is Miami or AIJ’s own. No YouTube creator footage, no Cuba, no taco stereotype, no one dragged, no blurred client, no woman in the white blouse.
Little Haiti and Little Havana shots carry the stakes line. Hotline shots C9068 and C9083 carry “For three decades”.
Sui starts with no pause, and her second half is covered with Miami.
Captions spell Americans for Immigrant Justice in full, Kelleher and Catherine Cassidy right.

decisions.b: The client script now reads “ten and half times more likely to win their case”. The narration in the cut says “ten times”. Andrés did not flag it. Nick or Atdhe confirms which line the gala hears.
The Deadline column is empty. The gala is Saturday 7 Nov. Nick sets the date for this version.
House rule adds the hook text over Cheryl’s opening bite. Andrés approved the opener without text. Keep it unless Andrés asks for a clean open.
